title: Code map: a git read whose empty result contradicts a held precondition is retried once, then indeterminate (DEC-299 a5)
description: opum-doc DEC-299 (a5), quoted verbatim: 'A git read whose empty result contradicts a precondition glyph already holds (a path known to match, an object known to exist) is suspect. glyph retries it once; if it is still empty, glyph returns indeterminate (exit 7, error envelope naming the read). It never returns a silent empty. Reads where empty is a legitimate answer are unchanged. Audit every git read in codemap.ts. Prove it on the SHIPPED runtime: node running dist/glyph.js under load, both ways. A forced empty read gives a retry then exit 7; a genuine empty read still answers. This BLOCKS the 0.1.0 tag.' Finding B of GCLI-51: git grep exit 0 with empty stdout and stderr gave lineRanges [] with no budget row. Scope: src/codemap.ts only; the src/git.ts reads (gitRun, ls-files, cat-file --batch) are out of scope and listed in the PR.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the PR lists every git read in src/codemap.ts with whether empty is legitimate or contradicts a held precondition

a contradicting empty read is retried once and then raises an indeterminate error (exit 7) naming the read; a legitimate empty read is unchanged (proof: tests both ways, including the quoted-path src/café.ts grep that exits 1 legitimately)
the spawn is injectable with the real spawn as the default and the seam is not reachable from the CLI (proof: a test and the shipped build)
mutation proofs: removing the retry and removing the guard each turn a named test red

proof on the shipped runtime: node running the packed dist/glyph.js under load, with the load method, counts, node version and SHA recorded, forced empty gives a retry then exit 7 and a genuine empty still answers
Opus review at the exact head before landing

implementationNotes: 2026-11-23 NODE MEASUREMENT for DEC-299 (a5) (worker, local macOS, 10 cores). OBJECT MEASURED: the packed Node bundle dist/glyph.js built by 'npm run build' from commit 8ff960b (fix(GCLI-56)), run by node v24.22.2 (not bun). LOAD: 150 busy 'while :; do :; done' sh loops (15x cores). HARNESS: a git wrapper first on PATH logs every git invocation (class, exit, stdout bytes) of the node-run glyph, and each run's stdout and exit code are compared with a baseline taken before the run set (two baseline runs equal). Per run: 'glyph code-map --source-ref main --json' (stdin task text naming a path, 3 identifiers and a plain token; exercises rev-parse, cat-file, merge-base, diff, grep -l, grep -n and the index build) and 'glyph callers helper07 --json' (exercises ls-files and cat-file --batch in src/git.ts), each with a fresh GLYPH_CACHE_DIR. RESULT, 60 runs x 2 commands = 120 command runs, 1500 git reads (rev-parse 300, cat-file 120, merge-base 60, diff names 120, diff ranges 240, grep -l 180, grep -n 240, ls-files 60, cat-file --batch 60, other 120): 0 reads with exit 0 and empty stdout at the git level (baseline also has 0 legitimate empties in this repo), 0 outputs differing from the baseline, 0 exit 7, 0 other exits. DETECTABLE RATE: 0 of 1500 reads and 0 of 120 command runs; by the rule of three the 95% upper bound is about 2e-3 per read and 2.5% per command run, so the sample could NOT have shown a fault rarer than about 1 in 500 reads; the bun-run fault measured earlier (9 events in 40 parity runs on bun 1.3.14) could not be called absent on node at that resolution if it were an order of magnitude rarer here. LIMITS: the wrapper adds a shell layer to every spawn, which may itself change timing; one scratch repo of 25 files; load is on this Mac, not the CI runner. POSITIVE CONTROLS (3 runs each, idle, same harness): pre-guard bundle (ef3fbe1) with ONE forced empty grep -n read: output silently diverged from the baseline in 3 of 3 code-map runs (the harness sees the fault); same for grep -l (3 of 3); the guarded bundle with the same single forced empty: 6 of 6 identical, the read executed twice (grep -n reads 15 vs 12 without the guard); guarded bundle with EVERY grep -n read empty: exit 7 in 3 of 3 code-map runs (callers unaffected, identical); forcing ls-files empty on the pre-guard bundle gave a non-zero exit in 3 of 6 command runs, i.e. an error, not a silent result. GENUINE EMPTY still answers: code-map with a task naming no repository token (grep -l exits 1) exits 0 with a result. RULE (opum-doc clarification to DEC-299 a5): ZERO empties observed under node, so (a5) stays at src/codemap.ts and the src/git.ts audit (gitRun, ls-files, cat-file --batch) is filed as a post-tag follow-up, subject to the leader/opum-doc reading of the detectable-rate limit above.

2026-11-23 REVIEW ROUND 1 (Opus, CHANGES, three blockers) FIXES at the head after 05e1534. (1) Retry tightened by ruling: a retry is accepted only if its stdout is non-empty; an exit-0-empty first read followed by an exit-1-empty retry is now exit 7 (tests for all six guarded reads). (2) The name-only/numstat pair: git prints a numstat row for every listed path (MEASURED on git 2.56.0, a scratch repo: a mode-only change gives name-only 'a.ts' and numstat '0<TAB>0<TAB>a.ts'; a binary file gives '-<TAB>-<TAB>c.bin'), so exactly one of the two empty is impossible; that one is retried once, then exit 7 naming it; both directions tested, plus the recover-on-retry cases and a mode-only no-false-positive case. (3) Legitimate empties asserted read ONCE: diff --unified=0 on a mode-only change (pointer kept, ranges []), merge-base exit 1 on an orphan source ref, cat-file non-zero for a named path absent at the ref, rev-parse exit 1 for an unknown ref (not_found, exit 3). Dead code `base.length === 0` removed. MUTATION PROOFS on the new head (src/codemap.ts mutated, tests/codemap-empty-read.test.ts run, restored): accepting the retry when it is not 'contradicting' -> 6 named tests red (one per guarded read); disabling the pair guard -> 4 red; disabling only the retry-still-empty throw in the pair guard -> 2 red. RESIDUAL: the guard tests emptiness only, so a transient TRUNCATED stdout still passes silently. NODE CONTROLS UNDER LOAD (B3): packed dist/glyph.js built by 'node scripts/build.mjs' from commit 7d6ebd5, node v24.22.2, git wrapper on PATH forcing 'git grep -n' empty, 30 busy sh loops (3x cores), code-map --source-ref origin/dev on this repo, fresh cache dir per run, 5 runs each: forced-empty on EVERY grep -n -> exit 7 in 5 of 5 ('git grep -n returned no output ... although the path matched'); forced-empty ONCE -> exit 0 with output byte-identical to the unloaded baseline in 5 of 5; genuine empty (task text naming no repository token) -> exit 0 with an answer in 5 of 5. NOTE: an earlier 150-loop attempt (15x cores) was discarded as a measurement of this: the code map spent its own 7000 ms time budget (a documented omission, 'time-budget: ... spent during symbol index'), so outputs differed from the baseline for that reason, not a guard fault; the forced-all runs that reached grep -n still gave exit 7. LIMITS: wrapper adds a shell layer; one repo; this Mac not the CI runner. The forced fault is injected, the real fault was measured on bun only.

2026-11-23 KNOWN EDGES AND RECORD CORRECTIONS (Opus round 2 APPROVE at 736993b; non-blocking items). RESIDUALS: (1) a retry that exits non-zero WITH output is accepted as an answer: rev-parse becomes not_found (exit 3), cat-file drops the named path, grep -l/-n status 1 gives []. The reviewer's reasoning, from git's behaviour and NOT measured here: git prints nothing to stdout on those failures, so this needs a compound fault; requiring retried.status === 0 as well would change the legitimate-negative handling of grep and cat-file, so the ruling stays as implemented. (2) If BOTH name-only and numstat fault empty together it is indistinguishable from 'no changes' and tier 2 is lost silently. (3) A transient TRUNCATED stdout still passes (recorded earlier). (4) The unit tests run with symbols:false, so the guard with tier 3 on is exercised only by the node controls. (5) The retry-nonzero message ('although it exited 0') drops the retry's status and stderr: diagnostic only. B3 RECORD: the earlier zero-event rate run used the 25-file scratch repo with --source-ref main and bundle 8ff960b; the controls above ran on glyph-cli itself with --source-ref origin/dev and bundle 7d6ebd5, so repo, load and bundle all differ from that run; the bigger repo's index build is the likely reason 150 loops spent the 7000 ms budget. 'Forced once, byte-identical 5/5' could pass vacuously with tier 3 on (symbol ranges merge with the grep -n lines), so the grep -n read count was recorded in a re-run (same bundle, 30 loops, 5 runs): unforced baseline 10 grep -n reads, forced-once 11 in 5 of 5 runs (the extra read is the retry), output byte-identical to the baseline in 5 of 5; forced-all exit 7 in 5 of 5. The pair tests now include a fresh mode-only branch and a binary-file case (both read once, not retried).
finalSummary: Landed as opum-ai/glyph-cli#112 (squash fa80b3e). AC 6 (Opus review at the exact landed head) left unchecked: round 2 APPROVE was recorded at 736993b and the landed head was 3a43a9f; not proven here.
